rationale: Instrumented the one path that used to abort the sweep so that a mis-ordered configuration change becomes data instead of a crash: the per-step apply now runs each committed EntryConfChangeV2 under a recover and counts a rejection in a new invalid_change_applies counter, reported in invariant_sweep_summary. This is the prerequisite for re-enabling configuration events aimed at an existing serving voter, which is the last item the open gap names: with the counter in place, a lag-driven mis-ordering would show up as a number rather than killing the run, and a zero would say the guard kept such changes out. The draft-side run reports the same counters as the executed revision plus invalid_change_applies=0 (elections=470, ordinary proposals=461, conf_change_proposals=262, restarts=429, unapplied_conf_change_states=48, stalled_states=0, violations=0), which is consistent with the propose-time alreadyPending/alreadyJoint rewrite documented in the knowledge recorded last turn; the experiment below asks for isolated execution so that zero is receipt-backed before it is used.

scope.description: Tenth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A-C and the deterministic joint-change case are unchanged. The sweep's per-step apply now calls applyConfChange for each committed EntryConfChangeV2 inside a recover-guarded closure and counts a recovered rejection in invalid_change_applies, which invariant_sweep_summary reports alongside seeds, steps, elections, ordinary proposals, conf_change_proposals, restarts, unapplied_conf_change_states, stalled_states and violations. The event set is otherwise the same as the executed revision: four real state machines with node 4 starting outside the configuration, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals on node 4 half of them JointImplicit, application lag that skips one node's apply about one time in six, restarts rebuilt from persisted hard state and applied ConfState, and the liveness witness with its antecedent counter.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState); no production logic is modified.
A recovered applyConfChange rejection means the node was handed a change its own tracker rejects; the counter does not claim the cause, only the occurrence.
The counter is the prerequisite for aiming configuration events at an existing serving voter, which is not yet enabled in this revision.
Randomness is fixed per seed; counts are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup, MsgProp, tick(), isolate, recover, TransferLeader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change on node 4, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (skipping one node about one time in six, and applying committed conf changes under recover, counting rejections), then evaluate the four invariants and the liveness witness, finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary with all counters including invalid_change_applies.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with the apply-side mis-ordering instrumented: committed conf changes are applied under recover and a rejection increments invalid_change_applies, which the summary now reports. This is the prerequisite for the still-open demotion variant of the configuration events. Fresh execution is requested because the harness bytes and the reported fields changed; a draft-side run reported invalid_change_applies=0 with the other counters unchanged, which is construction feedback only.
